deck.title: What was the Impact of Stalin's Economic Policies?

front_blocks.md: Define **Five-Year Plans**.

back_blocks.md: The **Five-Year Plans** were Stalin's economic programmes, introduced in 1928, that aimed to rapidly **industrialise** the USSR by setting economic targets over five-year intervals.

cards.front_md: Define **Five-Year Plans**.
cards.back_md: The **Five-Year Plans** were Stalin's economic programmes, introduced in 1928, that aimed to rapidly **industrialise** the USSR by setting economic targets over five-year intervals.

front_blocks.md: Define **Gosplan**.

back_blocks.md: **Gosplan** was the 'State Committee for Planning' that Stalin created to organise the Five-Year Plans, setting targets for each region, factory, manager and worker.

front_blocks.md: Define **Stakhanovite movement**.

back_blocks.md: The **Stakhanovite movement** was a campaign, named after Aleksei Stakhanov, that encouraged Soviet workers to exceed their production quotas.

front_blocks.md: Define **Collectivisation**.

back_blocks.md: **Collectivisation** was Stalin's policy, introduced in 1928, of combining individual farms into large collective farms to increase agricultural productivity.

front_blocks.md: Define **Kolkhoz**.

back_blocks.md: A **Kolkhoz** was a collective-owned farm on which members received a share of the farm's output and profit based on the days they worked.

front_blocks.md: Define **Sovkhoz**.

back_blocks.md: A **Sovkhoz** was a state-owned farm on which peasants were salaried workers paid a wage, with all decisions made by government officials.

front_blocks.md: Define **Holodomor**.

back_blocks.md: The **Holodomor** means 'death by hunger' and refers to the famine in Ukraine caused when the government took all the food from peasants who could not meet their grain quota.
